//! 🧬️ Architect program artifact — document mutation dispatch enum.
//!
//! Semantic vocabulary derived from `🗄️registers/🦀️.rs`'s ~65 generic per-collection
//! add/remove/patch registers plus the three document-level meta facets, per
//! `.🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️08/☀️12/SEMANTIC-MUTATIONS-OVERHAUL/📓️taxonomy.md`/`📓️derivation-rules.md`:
//! each header-shaped id-keyed register (rule 2) becomes `create`/`delete`/`rename`/`replace`;
//! the two edge-shaped registers (`adjacencies`, `traces` — rule 4) become `connect`/`disconnect`;
//! the three document-level scalar facets (`meta`/`project`/`governance` — rule 1) become
//! `rename`/`replace`. The old whole-document-replace variant is deleted outright (banned per
//! taxonomy — whole-document replace is not an in-history mutation; it goes through
//! `ArtifactStore::reset`).
//!
//! `#[derive(dsl::Mutations)]` generates `impl protocol::Mutation<ProgramSnapshot>` and
//! `impl protocol::SemanticMutation<ProgramSnapshot>` for `ProgramMutation` by delegating each
//! variant to its payload's `protocol::MutationKind` impl — see the triad leaves
//! (`<slug>/{🦠️mutation,🔺️diff,↩️inverse}`) for the handcrafted logic. This file is dispatch-only;
//! the old hand-written `apply_program_mutation`/`inverse_program_mutation`/`impl Mutation` are
//! deleted, replaced by the derive.
//!
//! Physical ownership is declared by the exact `mutationDomainOwners` taxonomy registry:
//! 69 domains contain 266 operation triads, such as `👥️stakeholder/🌱️create` and
//! `👥️stakeholder/🗑️delete`. Each triad retains its full mutation semantic ID and an
//! individual `#[path]` mount. Dispatch coverage compares variants and triad owners
//! bijectively through that registry.

use crate::ProgramDiff;
use crate::ProgramSnapshot;

//#region 🔖️ProgramMutation
/// 🧩️ Every variant wraps exactly one `protocol::MutationKind<ProgramSnapshot, ProgramMutation>`
/// payload struct declared in the corresponding triad leaf's `🦠️mutation/🦀️.rs`.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, dsl::ToValue, dsl::FromValue, dsl::Mutations)]
#[cfg_attr(test, derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
#[value(tag = "mutation", rename_all = "camelCase")]
#[cfg_attr(test, serde(tag = "mutation", rename_all = "camelCase"))]
#[mutations(snapshot = ProgramSnapshot, diff = ProgramDiff, schema = "s.architect.program")]
pub enum ProgramMutation {
    CreateInformationRequirement(super::create_information_requirement::CreateInformationRequirement),
    DeleteInformationRequirement(super::delete_information_requirement::DeleteInformationRequirement),
    RenameInformationRequirement(super::rename_information_requirement::RenameInformationRequirement),
    ReplaceInformationRequirement(super::replace_information_requirement::ReplaceInformationRequirement),
    CreateSustainabilityRequirement(super::create_sustainability_requirement::CreateSustainabilityRequirement),

/// 🧮️ Applies `mutation` to `snapshot` and hands back the whole `protocol::MutationOutcome`, the
/// diagnostics included — the shape an external conformance host needs, since a committed
/// `🎯️outcome` vector declares a status AND its diagnostic codes. This facet is dispatch-only and
/// has never carried an apply helper of its own; every in-crate caller goes through
/// `store::ArtifactStore`, which an external host cannot construct.
// 🚫️async: E1 pure computation over an in-memory snapshot, consumed from a synchronous external test host — see R9
pub fn apply_program_mutation_outcome(snapshot: &mut ProgramSnapshot, mutation: &ProgramMutation) -> protocol::MutationOutcome<ProgramDiff> {
    let outcome = <ProgramMutation as protocol::Mutation<ProgramSnapshot>>::diff(mutation, snapshot);
    outcome.apply_to(snapshot)
}

/// ↩️ `mutation`'s own inverse against `base`, as the step LIST `protocol::Mutation::inverse`
/// returns. Reachable from outside this crate, which `protocol::Mutation` itself is not — the
/// `protocol` extern-crate alias is private to `🦀️.rs`.
// 🚫️async: E1 pure computation over an in-memory snapshot, consumed from a synchronous external test host — see R9
pub fn inverse_program_mutation_steps(mutation: &ProgramMutation, base: &ProgramSnapshot) -> Vec<ProgramMutation> {
    <ProgramMutation as protocol::Mutation<ProgramSnapshot>>::inverse(mutation, base)
}

/// 📥️ Decodes the internally-tagged (`{"mutation": "<camelCaseVariant>", …}`) projection the
/// committed `<slug>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/🦠️mutation/🔣️.json` vectors carry.
// 🚫️async: E1 pure codec helper (file verified I/O-free) — see R9
pub fn decode_program_mutation_json(text: &str) -> Result<ProgramMutation, String> {
    dsl::json::from_json_str(text).map_err(|error| error.to_string())
}

/// 📥️ Decodes a committed `📸️snapshot/{⬅️before,➡️after}/🔣️.json` vector.
// 🚫️async: E1 pure codec helper (file verified I/O-free) — see R9
pub fn decode_program_snapshot_json(text: &str) -> Result<ProgramSnapshot, String> {
    dsl::json::from_json_str(text).map_err(|error| error.to_string())
}

/// 📤️ The snapshot as the same canonical JSON the committed vectors are written in — the
/// projection an external test host compares through.
// 🚫️async: E1 pure codec helper (file verified I/O-free) — see R9
pub fn encode_program_snapshot_json(snapshot: &ProgramSnapshot) -> String {
    dsl::json::to_json_string(snapshot)
}

[package]
workspace = "../../../.."
name = "semio-hub-procedural"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true
rust-version.workspace = true
description = "Procedural plugin composition for independently packaged generation2d and generation3d artifacts"

[lints]
workspace = true

[package.metadata.component]
package = "semio:procedural"

[package.metadata.semio]
deployment-directory = "🌀️procedural"
component-kind = "plugin"
role = "hub"
consumes = ["forms.questionKind", "flow.extension"]
depends-on = [
  "flow-extension-bim",
  "flow-extension-brep",
  "flow-extension-dictionary",
  "flow-extension-draw",
  "flow-extension-list",
  "flow-extension-logic",
  "flow-extension-math",
  "flow-extension-primitive",
  "flow-extension-text",
]

[[package.metadata.semio.playground]]
variant = "generation2d"
app = "s.procedural.generation2d@1/*#editor"
aliases = ["procedural 2d"]
ports = { react = 6021, wgpu = 6121 }

[[package.metadata.semio.playground]]
variant = "generation3d"
app = "s.procedural.generation3d@1/*#editor"
aliases = ["procedural 3d"]
ports = { react = 6018, wgpu = 6118 }

# 🎪️ The `generator` demonstrator row moved to
# ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🎪️demonstrator/🪪️manifest/🗿️artifact/⚡️implementations/🦀️rust/Cargo.toml — see that
# crate's docstring (REDUCE-DEMONSTRATOR-IDLE-MEMORY-FOOTPRINT).

[lib]
crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]
path = "../../🦀️.rs"

[features]
# 🔌️ The WASM component entry point (`plugin_exports!` → `#[no_mangle]`
# `semio_plugin_install_bundle`). Default-on so this plugin builds as its own component, and
# switched OFF by any crate that EMBEDS it (the 🎪️demonstrator bundles all six panes into one
# component): seven crates each exporting the same `#[no_mangle]` symbol is a duplicate-symbol
# link error, and the embedding crate is the one that must own the entry point.
default = ["plugin-entry"]
plugin-entry = []
# 🧮️ Installs `semio_framework_trace::HeapWitness` as this component's `#[global_allocator]` and
# thereby arms the reactor's per-turn retention trace. Diagnostic builds only — see the static's doc.
guest-heap-witness = ["dep:semio-framework-trace"]

[dependencies]
semio-framework-async = { path = "../../../../../🧰️framework/🔨️modules/⏳️async/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-ui-locale = { path = "../../../../../🧰️framework/🔨️modules/🖱️ui/🌐️locale/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-value = { path = "../../../../../🧰️framework/🔨️modules/🌱️value/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-s-artifact-procedural-generation2d = { workspace = true, features = ["component-app-assembly"] }
semio-s-artifact-procedural-generation3d = { workspace = true, features = ["component-app-assembly"] }
semio-framework-dispatch-macros = { workspace = true }
semio-framework-os-kernel = { workspace = true }
semio-framework-plugin = { workspace = true, features = ["component-guest"] }
# ⏯️ `dyn_enum_close!` copies `PluginApp::tool_run_trace_delta`'s signature verbatim into the generated

[package]
workspace = "../../../.."
name = "semio-hub-cad"

description = "CAD plugin - one crate for the cad artifact (diff/op/dsl/pack/spr/engine) and the cad play app (commands/modes/windows/panels)"

[lints]
workspace = true

[package.metadata.component]
package = "semio:cad"

[package.metadata.semio]
deployment-directory = "📐️cad"
component-kind = "plugin"
role = "hub"
consumes = ["cad.computer"]

# 📖️ Opts this plugin into the generated Storybook scope registry (`.storybook/📖️stories/🧭️coordination/🟦️.ts`'s
# `GENERATED_SCOPES`, read via `readSemioMarkerSubTable`) instead of a hand-maintained entry — see
# 26/08/06/GENERATED-STORYBOOK-SCOPES-AND-STORIES-FROM-PACKAGE-CATALOG. `sourceRoots` are relative to
# this plugin's OWNER dir (`✏️s/🔌️plugins/📐️cad`), matching the pre-existing hand-curated `cad` scope.
[package.metadata.semio.storybook]
id = "cad"
titlePrefix = "📐️cad"
sourceRoots = ["🗿️artifacts/📐️cad/🏅️standards/🔖️1/🪆️subsets/✳️any/✏️editor/⚙️engine/📺️renderer", "🗿️artifacts/📐️cad/🏅️standards/🔖️1/🪆️subsets/✳️any/📚️examples/🖼️assets"]
storyGlobs = ["📖️stories/**/🧪️.story.tsx"]

[[package.metadata.semio.playground]]
variant = "cad"
app = "s.cad.cad@1/*#editor"
ports = { react = 6020, wgpu = 6120 }

# 🎪️ The `koordinator` demonstrator row moved to
# ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🎪️demonstrator/🪪️manifest/🗿️artifact/⚡️implementations/🦀️rust/Cargo.toml — see that
# crate's docstring (REDUCE-DEMONSTRATOR-IDLE-MEMORY-FOOTPRINT). The `/cad-assets` asset row below
# stays here too (a copy also lives on the bundle crate) since the standalone `cad` dev variant needs
# it independently of the demonstrator.
[[package.metadata.semio.assets]]
kind = "static-dir"
route = "/cad-assets"
app = "s.cad.cad@1/*#editor"
root = "✏️s/🔌️plugins/📐️cad/🗿️artifacts/📐️cad/🏅️standards/🔖️1/🪆️subsets/✳️any/📚️examples/🖼️assets"

[lib]
crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]
path = "🦀️.rs"

[features]
# 🔌️ The WASM component entry point (`plugin_exports!` → `#[no_mangle]`
# `semio_plugin_install_bundle`). Default-on so this plugin builds as its own component, and
# switched OFF by any crate that EMBEDS it (the 🎪️demonstrator bundles all six panes into one
# component): seven crates each exporting the same `#[no_mangle]` symbol is a duplicate-symbol
# link error, and the embedding crate is the one that must own the entry point.
default = ["plugin-entry"]
plugin-entry = []

[dependencies]
semio-framework-value = { path = "../../../../../🧰️framework/🔨️modules/🌱️value/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }

[package]
workspace = "../../../.."
name = "semio-hub-demonstrator"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true
rust-version.workspace = true
description = "Entwerfen mit Bestand demonstrator plugin - one crate bundling the six demonstrator panes (generator/koordinator/aggregator/aussuchen/bearbeiten/verfolgen) served by procedural/cad/puzzle/sourcing/process/gis into one wasm component"

[lints]
workspace = true

[package.metadata.component]
package = "semio:demonstrator"

# 🎪️ REDUCE-DEMONSTRATOR-IDLE-MEMORY-FOOTPRINT: bundles the six mit-bestand demonstrator panes'
# already-existing apps (generation3d, cad, puzzle3d, sourcing-curation, process3d, gis2d) into ONE
# wasm component instead of six — the framework/kernel SDK (`semio-framework-plugin`,
# `semio-framework-os`) is statically linked exactly once, and the six panes share one plugin
# worker/module via the existing `acquirePluginModule` lease pool (framework core `🟦️.ts`),
# instead of six separate workers each duplicating that linkage. Each source plugin
# (procedural/cad/puzzle/sourcing/process/gis) keeps its own standalone playground rows unchanged
# for its own non-demonstrator variants (e.g. `generation3d`, `puzzle3d`) — only the six
# demonstrator-specific rows (`generator`/`koordinator`/`aggregator`/`aussuchen`/`bearbeiten`/`verfolgen`)
# live here.
[package.metadata.semio]
deployment-directory = "🎪️demonstrator"
component-kind = "plugin"
role = "hub"
consumes = ["forms.questionKind", "process.machines", "cad.computer", "sourcing.module", "flow.extension"]
# 🔗️ Runtime actor dependencies — the six plugins whose editor/viewer surfaces this crate registers
# over THEIR artifact kinds (`🪪️manifest/🎪️demonstrator/🦀️.rs`'s `.depends_on(…)` rows must match the
# plugin ids below exactly). Flow extensions are listed explicitly (not `flow.extension`) so the
# mit-bestand build does not materialize `flow-extension-draw`, which generation3d does not use.
# `stdio` is deliberately absent: every `semio_s_artifact_stdio_*` call here is an in-process codec
# call into a linked rlib, not a message to a separate stdio actor.
depends-on = [
  "cad",
  "gis",
  "procedural",
  "process",
  "puzzle",
  "sourcing",
  "flow-extension-bim",
  "flow-extension-brep",
  "flow-extension-dictionary",
  "flow-extension-list",
  "flow-extension-logic",
  "flow-extension-math",
  "flow-extension-primitive",
  "flow-extension-text",
]

# reach into the OS host crate to register `"3d.cad"`'s ten solid/mesh/dwg codecs and `"2d.map"`'s
# two media codecs — kinds it neither declares nor owns — making plugin load order decide the winner
# for a process-global key. Those registrations now live with 📐️cad and 🌍️gis, so this crate needs
# neither the host crate nor the BRep kernel it passed to it. `POLICY_PLUGIN_DEP_OS_SYMBOLS` carries
# no carve-out for `🎪️demonstrator` any more: reintroducing the dependency is a plain breach.

# crate bundles all six into ONE component and owns the single `semio_plugin_install_bundle`
# entry point. Without this, seven crates export that `#[no_mangle]` symbol and the component
# fails to link with duplicate-symbol errors.

semio-s-artifact-puzzle-3d = { workspace = true, features = ["component-app-assembly"] }

# supplies only the protocol, the runner and the adapter API. If a dependency ever appears here, the
# framework has started to know about an implementation.

manifests.name: obj-3-0-any-fixture-generator
manifests.source:
# 🧭️ Own workspace root: linked by `../📜️script.ts` (`cargo build --manifest-path`), never joins the
# repository's root workspace, whose root manifest is a shared, contended file.
#
# Builds this subset's `third-party-generated` fixture and ADMITS it with the SAME registered
# reference crate (`tobj` 4) named in `../../🔣️oracle.json`'s `tobj-obj-3-0-mutate` oracle —
# never with this repository's own `encode_obj`/`decode_obj`. OBJ has no reference WRITER in the
# Rust ecosystem (`tobj` is read-only), which is the already-recorded reason this subset's oracle
# writes the grammar itself and uses `tobj` as the independent reader; the generator mirrors exactly
# that precedent. See `../📜️script.ts` for the generation contract.
[workspace]

[package]
name = "obj-3-0-any-fixture-generator"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
publish = false

[[bin]]
name = "generate"
path = "../../🦀️.rs"

[dependencies]
tobj = "4"

manifests.name: tobj-obj-reader
manifests.source:
# 🧭️ Own workspace root, exactly like this ticket's other scratch/oracle crates and the sibling
# `🦀️engine` directory in this same folder — never joins the repository's root workspace or its
# Cargo.lock.
#
# This is the READER wrapper the `tobj-obj-3-0-mutate-reader` oracle (`../../🔣️oracle.json`)
# points at. It depends on nothing but the real `tobj` 4 — the exact crate registered there — and is
# never invoked to compute what a mutation SHOULD produce (that stays this subset's own
# `🦀️oracle.rs`, a DIFFERENT, `cross-semio-implementation`-registered mechanism). This
# crate only builds fixture bytes (hand-authored grammar, mirroring the sibling `🦀️engine`'s own
# precedent — OBJ has no reference WRITER in the Rust ecosystem) and projects real bytes back out
# through `tobj`'s own reading — the mechanism `../../🔬️probes/📜️script.ts` shells out to.
[workspace]

[package]
name = "tobj-obj-reader"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
publish = false

[[bin]]
name = "tobj-obj-reader"
path = "../../🦀️.rs"

[dependencies]
tobj = "4"

manifests.name: semio-framework-os-kernel
manifests.source:
[package]
workspace = "../../../../.."
name = "semio-framework-os-kernel"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version.workspace = true
description = "Semio framework OS kernel — wasm-safe store/spr/dsl/pack document model"

[package.metadata.semio]
channel-version-consumers = "🧫️fixtures/📡️channel/📇️consumers.json"
role = "framework"
id = "os-kernel"

[lints]
workspace = true

[lib]
name = "semio_framework_os_kernel"
crate-type = ["rlib", "cdylib"]
path = "🦀️.rs"

[[test]]
name = "pack_schema_hash"
path = "../../🔨️modules/🎒️pack/🌱️value/🧪️tests/🔬️schema-hash/🦀️.rs"

[[test]]
name = "sqlite_snapshot_native_admission"
path = "../../🔨️modules/🏪️store/📦️codec/🪶️snapshot-capability/🪶️native-decoding/🧪️tests/🚪️public/🦀️.rs"

[features]
protocol-laws = ["record-codec-laws"]
record-codec-laws = ["semio-framework-pack/corruption-testing"]
durable-group-testing = []
default = ["deflate"]
deflate = ["semio-framework-replication/deflate", "semio-framework-pack/deflate"]
# 🌀️ MICROKERNEL-POOLED-ACTOR-PLUGIN-RUNTIME (packet terra-directory-and-run): the native
# `📇️directory/🔌️client`'s `NativeDirectoryTransport` routes its HTTP calls through
# `semio-framework-os-services`'s `HttpPool`/`ComputePool` (bounded, cancellable, deadline-aware).
# The services edge now belongs to `sync` as the shared host boundary for Store file watching too.
ureq = ["dep:ureq", "dep:semio-framework-actor"]
# 🧵️ No `tokio/net` reference here (unlike `rt`/`time`): `tokio` is now a
# `not(all(target_arch = "wasm32", target_env = "p2"))`-gated dependency (presentation on native and
# browser wasm32, absent from wasip2), so a feature-flag `tokio/net` would still unify onto browser
# wasm32, and tokio's own build script hard-errors on `net` for wasm32 (unlike `rt`/`time`, which it
# explicitly supports there). `net` is instead added unconditionally for non-wasm32 targets only, via
# the `[target.cfg(not(wasm32))]` `tokio` entry below — see its docstring. WASI-P2 guest plugins
# never link the sync actor's native (tokio-tungstenite) transport — see `🔄️sync/🦀️.rs`'s
# `native_actor` vs `wasm_actor` split — so `net` has no business reaching wasm32 at all.
sync = ["dep:tokio-tungstenite", "dep:semio-framework-os-services", "dep:ureq", "tokio/rt", "tokio/time"]
worker = ["sync"]
# 🧬️ Keeps the boundary/protocol type-generation capability explicit at this layer. The current
# wire declarations are owned by `semio-framework`, so enabling this feature adds no dependency.
typegen = []
# ⌨️ The native command-line binaries (`pack`, `spr`, `semio`). Their `cli` modules are mounted only
# off wasm32 (`os_pack::cli`, `os_spr::cli` need the native file layer), so the bins are opt-in: a
# wasm32 test build of this crate (`--target wasm32-wasip2 --test pack_schema_hash`) never tries to
# link them, and a native caller asks for them with `--features native-bin`.
native-bin = []

[dependencies]
semio-framework-pack-json = { path = "../../../../🔨️modules/🎒️pack/🔤️json/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-diagnostic = { path = "../../../../🔨️modules/⚠️diagnostic/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-dsl = { path = "../../../../🔨️modules/🗣️dsl/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-ui-locale = { path = "../../../../🔨️modules/🖱️ui/🌐️locale/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-schema-state = { path = "../../../../🔨️modules/🧬️schema/📶️state/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-schema-composition = { path = "../../../../🔨️modules/🧬️schema/🧩️composition/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-schema-validator = { workspace = true }
semio-framework-value = { path = "../../../../🔨️modules/🌱️value/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
dsl_derive = { path = "../../🔨️modules/🗣️dsl/✨️derive/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-os-kernel-dsl-derive" }
semio-framework-value-derive = { path = "../../../../🔨️modules/🌱️value/✨️derive/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-value-derive" }
semio-framework-pack = { workspace = true }
semio-framework-replication = { workspace = true }
semio-framework-schema-registry = { workspace = true }
semio-framework-ui-viewport = { workspace = true }
# 🪪️ `OperationContext`/`CancelToken`/`ScopeHandle` vocabulary (ticket
# 26/08/17/MICROKERNEL-POOLED-ACTOR-PLUGIN-RUNTIME) — pure, zero-tokio, wasm32-safe, so this is an
# unconditional (not target-gated) dependency: `📇️directory/🔌️client`'s `DirectoryTransport` trait
# carries an `OperationContext` on every implementation, native AND browser alike.
semio-framework-async = { workspace = true, features = ["entrypoint"] }
# 🔤️ `pack_value_to_base64`/`pack_value_from_base64` (`🏪️store/🦀️.rs`) are the only base64
# call sites this crate owns, and they are genuinely guest-reachable (scene `*Json` field encoding),
# not host-only — so this re-points at the first-party RFC 4648 codec instead of target-gating a
# third-party dependency away. Replaces the former `base64 = "0.22.1"` entry.
semio-framework-io-base64 = { path = "../../../../🔨️modules/🚪️io/🔤️base64/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
serde = { version = "1.0.219", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1.0.140"
semio-framework-hash = { path = "../../../../🔨️modules/🔏️hash/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-hash" }
semio-framework-job = { workspace = true }
# 🧮️ `GUEST_CONTIGUOUS_REQUEST_CEILING_BYTES`/`GUEST_HOST_ANSWER_CEILING_BYTES` — the one declared
# linear-memory budget `📡️spr/🧵️channel`'s paged command ingress derives its page and byte
# authorities from, so no transport here re-chooses a ceiling the guest allocator already fixes.
# Zero-dependency, pure std, wasm32-wasip2-safe (the guest plugin crate already links it).
semio-framework-trace = { workspace = true }

# 🌉️ Browser-only bridges reached through this crate's mounted modules (`🪪️identity`'s
# `crypto.getRandomValues` entropy arm, `📇️directory/🔌️client`'s experimental `browser` transport,
# `🏪️store/🔄️sync`'s `wasm_actor`, `🏪️store/👷️worker`'s Web Worker `postMessage` bridge) plus the
# `wasm_bindgen_futures` alias their async-fn codegen needs. Excluded from `wasm32-wasip2` because
# `target_arch = "wasm32"` is TRUE for the WASI component target too. `fill_entropy`/`now_ms`
# needed genuine wasip2 arms instead — see their docstrings.
[target.'cfg(all(target_arch = "wasm32", not(target_env = "p2")))'.dependencies]
js-sys = "0.3.83"
wasm-bindgen = "0.2.106"
web-sys = { version = "0.3.98", features = ["Window", "Storage", "console", "WebSocket", "MessageEvent", "CloseEvent", "BinaryType", "Request", "RequestInit", "Response", "Headers"] }

# 🧵️ Host-only tokio + zip, presentation on native AND browser wasm32, absent only from the shipped
# `wasm32-wasip2` component target — `target_arch = "wasm32"` is TRUE for wasm32-wasip2 too, so the
# full `not(all(target_arch = "wasm32", target_env = "p2")))` form is required (see the module-level
# docstring on `[target.'cfg(all(target_arch = "wasm32", not(target_env = "p2")))'.dependencies]`
# above for why a bare arch gate is wrong). `tokio` backs the `sync` cargo feature's native
# `tokio-tungstenite` transport and (base `sync`/`macros` tokio features only) the browser
# `📇️directory/🔌️client::browser` WebSocket bridge's `tokio::sync::mpsc` channel — both entirely
# outside a WASI guest's reach (`🔄️sync/🦀️.rs`'s own docstring: "WASI-P2 plugins never link
# this crate ... This actor is a host-side concern only"; the browser bridge is
# `cfg(all(target_arch = "wasm32", not(target_env = "p2")))`-gated already). `semio-framework-deflate` (its first-party
# `zip_archive`) backs `🧩️extension`'s `.sxt` package pack/unpack/verify — installing a runtime extension is host tooling
# (only caller repo-wide: `semio-framework-os`'s native host crate), never something a guest
# component does to itself; its module mount is gated the same way in `🦀️.rs`.
[target.'cfg(not(all(target_arch = "wasm32", target_env = "p2")))'.dependencies]
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["sync", "macros"], default-features = false }
semio-framework-deflate = { path = "../../../../🔨️modules/🗜️deflate/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }

[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies]
futures = "0.3"
tokio-tungstenite = { version = "0.26", optional = true, features = ["rustls-tls-webpki-roots"] }
# 🧵️ Same crate key as the `not(all(target_arch = "wasm32", target_env = "p2"))` table above — cargo
# unifies same-name deps declared in multiple matching `[target.cfg(...)]` tables into one edge for
# a given target, unioning features (non-optional here to match that table's non-optional bit; a
# rename-alias or a mixed optional/non-optional pairing under one name both hit cargo's "multiple
# times with different names" / conflicting-optionality rejections). `net` is therefore always
# presentation for non-wasm32 builds of this crate, independent of the `sync` feature toggle — harmless
# (tokio without `sync`'s other deps never spins up a listener) and the only way to keep `net` off
# wasm32 unconditionally (both browser and wasip2), which is the actual requirement: no wasm32 target
# of this crate should ever link tokio's networking.
tokio = { version = "1", default-features = false, features = ["net"] }
# 🌀️ `HttpPool`/`ComputePool` and the owned file-change watcher. This remains optional because all
# consumers are native sync-runtime paths; this crate names only OS-services-owned types.
semio-framework-os-services = { workspace = true, optional = true }
# 🪪️ `PackageId`/`ActorId` — `HttpPool::request`'s own per-package/per-actor quota identity
# (`semio-framework-os-services`'s doc: "consumed from here rather than reinvented locally"). Pure,
# no tokio, but only the native `HttpPool`-backed transport constructs one, so it rides the same
# `ureq` feature as `semio-framework-os-services` above.
semio-framework-actor = { workspace = true, optional = true }
# 🌐️ The native `NativeDirectoryTransport`'s blocking HTTP client (rustls + ring). Every use site is
# `cfg(all(feature = "ureq", feature = "sync", not(target_arch = "wasm32")))`, and ring's `getrandom 0.2`
# does not build for browser wasm32, so the `sync`/`ureq` features name it as a native-only edge.
ureq = { version = "2", optional = true }

[[bin]]

semio-framework = { path = "../../../../../📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework" }
semio-framework-plugin = { path = "../../../🔨️modules/🔌️plugin/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-plugin" }
ui_wgpu = { path = "../../../../../🔨️modules/🖱️ui/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-ui", features = ["wgpu"] }
# 🚪️ `semio-framework-3d` dependency REMOVED (ticket 26/08/12/DISSOLVE-KERNELS-AND-MODULES-INTO-EVENT-SOURCED-ARTIFACTS
# wave IO1): the only references to it in this crate were `register_solid_exporter`/`register_solid_importer`
# and their supporting registry (`//#region SolidMediaExport`, `🖥️host/🦀️.rs`), deleted this same
# wave as dead weight with zero production callers. Verified with `grep -rn "semio_framework_3d"` across this
# crate's whole mounted input set (not just this directory) before removing the line.
serde = { version = "1.0.219", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1.0.140"
# 🔤️ `base64` (third-party, unconditional) REMOVED: all 13 call sites in `🖥️host/🦀️.rs`
# (`backbone`, `instance`, `media_export_raster`, `media_export_simple`, `workflow`) now use the
# first-party, byte-exact `semio-framework-io-base64` codec instead — base64 encode/decode is
# target-neutral pure computation, so it needed re-pointing, not a target-gate, matching
# os-kernel's proven `pack_value_to_base64`/`pack_value_from_base64` fix
# (`os-kernel-host-crates-split.md`).
base64_codec = { path = "../../../../../🔨️modules/🚪️io/🔤️base64/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-io-base64" }

# 🖼️ SVG parsing/rasterization is a native-host capability.  Keep its renderer stack out of a
# wasm32-wasip2 guest while retaining the target-neutral media registry.
[target.'cfg(not(all(target_arch = "wasm32", target_env = "p2")))'.dependencies]
semio-framework-pixels = { path = "../../../../../🔨️modules/🔲️pixels/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
resvg = "0.45.1"
tiny-skia = "0.11.4"
usvg = "0.45.1"
# 🗜️ `semio-framework-deflate` (its first-party `zip_archive`) is optional: its only production consumer is
# `🔨️modules/🪐️space/🦀️.rs`'s `//#region 🔖️Zip` (`export_collection_zip`/`import_collection_zip`
# and their `ZipStoreBridge`), which builds a portable `.zip` byte stream from caller-injected,
# already-in-memory bytes — zero ambient filesystem access, but genuinely host-only: it has no
# production caller anywhere in the repo today (its own docstring names its intended consumer as
# "a live `store::SpaceHost`'s registered members, W4's storage wave", a native host construct),
# and a WASI guest component has no reason to bundle its own export archive format. Same proof
# shape as `os-kernel`'s `os_extension` module (`os-kernel-host-crates-split.md`): `target_arch =
# "wasm32"` is TRUE for `wasm32-wasip2`, so this needs the full `not(all(...))` gate, not a bare
# `not(target_arch = "wasm32")` one.
semio-framework-deflate = { path = "../../../../../🔨️modules/🗜️deflate/📦️packages/🦀️rust", optional = true }

[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies]
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["sync"], default-features = false }
# 🎠️ MICROKERNEL-POOLED-ACTOR-PLUGIN-RUNTIME (packet `run-kernel-wiring`): this crate did not depend
# on the plugin-host runtime AT ALL before this packet, which is exactly why "native smoke" (33/33
# via `semio-framework-os-run`) exercised a code path the product does not use — `🎠️activation/🦀️.rs`'s
# own module doc explains the fix. Native-only: `NativeKernelRuntime` spawns real OS threads and is
# never compiled for wasm32, where the JS host already owns plugin execution off this crate.
semio-framework-actor = { workspace = true }
semio-framework-plugin-host = { path = "../../../🔨️modules/🔌️plugin/🖥️host/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-plugin-host" }
semio-framework-async = { workspace = true }

[dev-dependencies]
png = "0.17.16"
semio-framework-async-macros = { path = "../../../../../🔨️modules/⏳️async/✨️macros/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }

[features]
default = []
space-guest = ["dep:semio-framework-artifact-space-space", "dep:semio-framework-artifact-space-collection"]
os-host-full = ["space-guest", "dep:semio-framework-deflate", "semio-framework-os-kernel/sync"]

manifests.source:
[package]
workspace = "../../../../../../../../../.."
name = "semio-framework-os-renderer-wgpu"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version.workspace = true
description = "Raw wgpu WASM renderer for declarative framework UiNode trees"
build = "build.rs"


[package.metadata.semio]
role = "framework"
id = "renderer-wgpu"

[lints]
workspace = true
[lib]
crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]
path = "📚️library/🦀️.rs"

[target.'cfg(not(target_os = "wasi"))'.dependencies]
semio-framework-hash = { path = "../../../../../../../../../🔨️modules/🔏️hash/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
# ⏱️ P1e (INTERACTIVE-JOB-RUNTIME-REFACTOR, one-pool-worker-runtime): the interactivity watchdog
# (`Watchdog::start`) `winit_app.rs`'s `redraw()` wraps around every renderer frame callback — zero
# external deps, portable on the browser and native presentation targets. The WASI renderer build
# compiles only the target-neutral mailbox core and therefore does not need this presentation edge.
semio-framework-trace = { workspace = true }
# 🧵️ P3b (INTERACTIVE-JOB-RUNTIME-REFACTOR, ui-thread-isolation): `../../🧵️frame-job/🦀️.rs`'s `InteractiveJob`
# seam (`InteractiveJob`/`StepContext`/`StepOutcome`/`drive_step`/`run_to_completion`/`run_on_worker`,
# design ticket packet P2a) — portable on every target (`run_on_worker` itself, which needs
# `semio_framework_async::WorkerPool`, is only called from the native-only half of `frame_job.rs`; the
# job-protocol types used by the browser and native presentation module build clean on wasm32).
# Workspace-internal — `bun ./📜️script.ts verify dependencies` stays 238→238.
semio-framework-job = { workspace = true }
semio-framework-pixels = { path = "../../../../../../../../../🔨️modules/🔲️pixels/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
flow = { path = "../../../../../../🌊️flow/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-os-flow" }
semio-framework = { path = "../../../../../../../../../📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework" }
framework_surface_node_graph = { path = "../../../../../../../../../🔨️modules/🗺️surface/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-surface" }
framework_editor = { path = "../../../../../../../../../🔨️modules/✍️editor/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-editor" }
infinite_canvas = { path = "../../../../../../♾️infinite/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-os-infinite" }
# 🎬️ Direct dependency (rather than reaching through `infinite_world`, which imports these privately)
# so the Tutorial track's camera keyframes can convert to/from `OrbitController`/`Camera3d` — see
# `//#region 🎬️Tutorial` in lib.rs.
semio-framework-3d = { path = "../../../../../../../../../🔨️modules/🧊️3d/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-os-kernel = { path = "../../../../../../../📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-os-kernel" }
# 👕️ The replication contract's pure peer-overlay derivation (`peers_for_window`, `canvas_point_to_screen`, …) the wgpu
# canvas-presence twin (`🧱️elements/👕️canvas-presence/🎯️targets/🧊️wgpu`) paints peers with. Workspace-internal.
replication = { path = "../../../../../../../../../🔨️modules/📡️replication/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-replication" }
semio-framework-os-config = { workspace = true }
semio-framework-value = { workspace = true }
semio-framework-os-shell = { workspace = true }
# ⏪️ The time-travel session's own EN/DE stage and refusal labels (`TimeTravelLabel`) the shell's time-travel band
# reads, so the band and the Rust-built History body say the same words. Target-neutral, workspace-internal.
semio-framework-time-travel = { workspace = true }
# 🖊️ The drawing text line law (`drawing_text_lines`, `DRAWING_TEXT_LINE_HEIGHT`) the Canvas2d scene-node paint lays
# text out with — the very law React's `drawSceneNode` imports from `◻️2d`. Target-neutral, workspace-internal.
semio-framework-2d = { workspace = true }
ui_wgpu ={ path = "../../../../../../../../../🔨️modules/🖱️ui/📦️packages/🦀️rust", features = ["wgpu-engine"], package = "semio-framework-ui" }
semio-framework-ui-viewport = { path = "../../../../../../../../../🔨️modules/🖱️ui/🪟️viewport/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
# 🖥️ P3a (INTERACTIVE-JOB-RUNTIME-REFACTOR, ui-thread-isolation): `winit_app.rs`/`os_host.rs` already
# named `ui_host::{WindowDelegate, WindowMetrics, RedrawOutcome, should_request_redraw, PointerRegistry,
# pointer_info_for_mouse, ...}` throughout (the `os-host` packet's own `WindowDelegate for OsHost` seam),
# but this dependency line was missing — a real, pre-existing defect this crate's own build never
# surfaced because `cargo check -p semio-framework-os-renderer-wgpu` never reached this crate's files at
# all (blocked upstream by `semio-framework-2d`/`-graph`/`-ui` — see Phase 1 packet P1e's own report).
# Workspace-internal — `bun ./📜️script.ts verify dependencies` stays 238→238.
ui_host = { path = "../../../../../../../../../🔨️modules/🖱️ui/🖥️host/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-ui-host" }
# 🖼️ P3a: same missing-dependency defect as `ui_host` above — `os_host.rs`/`winit_app.rs`/`deadlines.rs`
# already named `ui_render::{FrameScheduler, InvalidationReason, DispatchEvent, CursorRequest, ...}`
# without this crate ever declaring the dependency. Workspace-internal, 238→238.
ui_render = { path = "../../../../../../../../../🔨️modules/🖱️ui/🖌️render/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-ui-render" }
# 🧬️ The renderer-neutral UI contract: `🐚️Shell/🎯️targets/🧊️wgpu` reads `ui_contract::FlowInline` for
# the shared anchored-overlay positioner (ticket 26/09/17 packet W2k). Workspace-internal, 238→238.
ui_contract = { path = "../../../../../../../../../🔨️modules/🖱️ui/🧬️contract/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-ui-contract" }
# 🎨️ Same undeclared-dependency shape once more — `🧱️elements/⚙️EngineCanvas/🎯️targets/🧊️wgpu/🦀️.rs`
# reads `ui_styling::metrics::label::LEGIBLE_MIN_PX` for its engine-surface label gate. Workspace-internal.
ui_styling = { path = "../../../../../../../../../🔨️modules/🖱️ui/🎨️styling/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-ui-styling" }
semio-framework-plugin = { path = "../../../../../../🔌️plugin/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-plugin" }
serde = { version = "1.0.219", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1.0.140"
base64 = "0.22.1"
# 🔤️ The first-party RFC 4648 codec `request_file_open` encodes a picked file with. Workspace-internal;
# it is what replaces the third-party `base64` crate on this crate's remaining data-url paths.
semio-framework-io-base64 = { path = "../../../../../../../../../🔨️modules/🚪️io/🔤️base64/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-io-base64" }
image = { version = "0.25", default-features = false, features = ["png", "jpeg"] }
vello = { version = "0.9.0", default-features = false, features = ["wgpu"] }
winit = { version = "0.30.12", default-features = false, features = ["rwh_06"] }
resvg = "0.45.1"
tiny-skia = "0.11.4"
usvg = "0.45.1"

# 🐧️ winit's Linux backends are features; these load their system libraries at run time (no dev packages).
[target.'cfg(target_os = "linux")'.dependencies]
winit = { version = "0.30.12", default-features = false, features = ["rwh_06", "x11", "wayland", "wayland-dlopen"] }
accesskit_winit = { version = "0.34.1", default-features = false, features = ["rwh_06", "accesskit_unix", "async-io"] }

[features]
native-bin = []

[[bin]]
name = "semio-wgpu-native"
path = "💾️binary/🦀️.rs"
required-features = ["native-bin"]

[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies]
semio-framework-schema = { workspace = true }
# 🖥️ Native-only: it embeds wasmtime, and its `wasmtime-wasi` pulls tokio/mio, which hard-fails on
# wasm32. Its only users here (`🎠️runtime`, `kernel_runtime`) are already `cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))`;
# the previous `not(target_os = "wasi")` gate admitted wasm32-unknown-unknown, whose target_os is "unknown".
semio-framework-plugin-host = { path = "../../../../../../🔌️plugin/🖥️host/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-plugin-host" }
# 🎭️ MICROKERNEL-POOLED-ACTOR-PLUGIN-RUNTIME (H3-wgpu-native): the `Kernel`/`ActorId`/`ThreadTransport`
# vocabulary the native kernel thread (`../../🧊️renderer/🦀️.rs`'s `kernel_runtime` module) drives directly — see
# `📓️terra-H3-wgpu-native-report.md`.
semio-framework-actor = { workspace = true }
# 🧵️ P1e (INTERACTIVE-JOB-RUNTIME-REFACTOR, one-pool-worker-runtime): `WorkerPool`/`worker_count_for`
# — `../../🧊️renderer/🦀️.rs::renderer_worker_pool()` is the ONE process-wide pool this crate injects into both
# `../../🎠️runtime/🦀️.rs`'s `ParallelRuntime` (shard-turn scheduling) and `Shell/🎯️targets/🧊️wgpu/🦀️.rs`'s
# `TokioHostRuntime` (directory-client HTTP work) — "the global thread budget exists so no component
# sizes itself per-CPU" (that fn's own doc), now literally one pool object rather than a per-caller
# sizing formula.
semio-framework-async = { workspace = true, features = ["entrypoint"] }
# 📇️ ticket 26/08/16/HUB-SPACES-LIVE-PRESENCE-AND-COLLABORATIVE-STUDIOS §C0/§C6 (lane 2-D):
# `os_directory::client::native::NativeDirectoryTransport` is supplied by the OS-kernel feature;
# the renderer never names its HTTP implementation dependency. `tokio`'s own `rt`/`net`/`time` are unified in from the
# kernel crate's own `sync` feature (`tokio-tungstenite`'s WS transport needs a real reactor), listed
# explicitly here too so this crate's own directory-stream background thread doesn't rely on that
# unification being implicit.
semio-framework-os-kernel = { path = "../../../../../../../📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-os-kernel", features = ["sync", "ureq"] }
# 🌀️ MICROKERNEL-POOLED-ACTOR-PLUGIN-RUNTIME (terra-directory-and-run): `TokioHostRuntime`/
# `ComputePool` — `🐚️Shell/🎯️targets/🧊️wgpu/🦀️.rs`'s directory-stream background thread used to build its OWN
# private `tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread()` reactor; that is retired in favour of ONE
# shared runtime managed from here, matching the confinement `semio-framework-os-services`'s own
# module doc describes ("the ONE crate allowed to name tokio").
semio-framework-os-services = { workspace = true }
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["sync", "rt", "net", "time"], default-features = false }
# ♿️ The native shell's platform accessibility bridge (`♿️native-accessibility`): the accessibility projection every window and
# the chrome publish becomes one macOS NSAccessibility / Windows UI Automation / Linux AT-SPI tree. Behind that one module —
# no public signature names an `accesskit` type (ticket 26/09/23 slice WG10). Linux adds its AT-SPI adapter below.
accesskit = "0.25.1"
accesskit_winit = { version = "0.34.1", default-features = false, features = ["rwh_06"] }

[target.'cfg(all(target_arch = "wasm32", target_os = "unknown"))'.dependencies]
# 🌉️ The browser half of the same crate the native half above already depends on: `🧊️renderer/🦀️.rs:2`
# aliases it as `wasm_bindgen_futures` for the wasm-bindgen expansion and `:122` imports
# `browser::spawn_local`, `🌉️ProgramBridge/🎯️targets/🧊️wgpu/🦀️.rs:19` imports `browser::JsFuture` and
# `🧵️frame-job/🦀️.rs:13` imports `Lane` — all four unresolved (`E0463`/`E0433`/`E0432`) because this
# dependency existed only under `cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))`, which is why the browser target
# never compiled. `entrypoint` stays OFF here: `block_on` must not be reachable from a browser build.
# Workspace-internal — `bun ./📜️script.ts verify dependencies` is unchanged.
semio-framework-async = { workspace = true }
# 📡️ The browser half of the document relay: `ArtifactHost` and the `store_sync::sync` vocabulary the
# shell's one `open_document` body names on both targets, plus the `broadcast` receiver it drains.
semio-framework-os-kernel = { path = "../../../../../../../📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-os-kernel", features = ["sync"] }
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["sync"], default-features = false }
getrandom = { version = "0.3.4", features = ["wasm_js"] }
js-sys = "0.3.83"
wasm-bindgen = "0.2.106"
web-sys = { version = "0.3.98", features = [
    "Window",

] }

manifests.source:
# 🧭️ Own workspace root: linked by `../📜️script.ts` (`cargo run --manifest-path`), never joins the
# repository's root workspace, whose root manifest is a shared, contended file.
#
# Builds this subset's `third-party-generated` fixtures with the SAME reference crate (`gif` 0.13)
# — never with this repository's own `encode_gif`. See `../📜️script.ts` for the generation contract.
#
# Two independent binaries, two independent oracles:
#   `generate` (src/main.rs)        — 🎬️pattern-strip.gif, untouched, backs the pre-existing
#                                     `gif-89a-any-mutate` CROSS-SEMIO oracle registration.
#   `reader`   (src/📖️reader_main.rs) — the per-kind before/after recipe corpus, backs the NEW
#                                     `gif-89a-any-mutate-reader` THIRD-PARTY-LIBRARY oracle. Its
#                                     `project` subcommand deliberately uses ONLY `gif::Decoder`'s
#                                     public getters — never the raw-block-scan technique
#                                     `🦀️oracle.rs` uses to fill the crate's read gaps —
#                                     so witnessability here is what a genuine reader can prove, not
#                                     what a second implementation can compute.
#
# 🧭️ Named `src/📖️reader_main.rs`, NOT Cargo's default `src/bin/reader.rs` convention: the repo root
# `.gitignore` has a blanket `[Bb]in/` rule (meant for build-output `bin/` dirs) that silently
# swallows anything under a `src/bin/` path too — confirmed with `git check-ignore`. Editing the
# shared root `.gitignore` is out of this subset's scope, so the file lives beside `main.rs`
# instead and `path` below points at it explicitly.
[workspace]

[package]
name = "gif-89a-any-fixture-generator"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
publish = false

[[bin]]
name = "generate"
path = "../../🦀️.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "reader"
path = "../../📖️reader/🦀️.rs"

[dependencies]
gif = "0.13"

# The EXTENSION-BLOCK reader. This subset's existing reader uses `gif`'s high-level `Decoder`, which
# models a decoded animation: comment (0xFE) and application (0xFF) extension blocks are consumed on
# the way to frames and never surfaced, which is why those kinds were `-uncarried` against it.
#
# `gif`'s documented low-level entry point (`streaming_decoder::StreamingDecoder`) emits
# `Decoded::SubBlockFinished(AnyExtension)` and exposes `last_ext()` -> (label, payload, is_end), so
# every extension block is observable by label and payload. Still the library's own reading, not ours.

manifests.source:
[package]
workspace = "../../../../../../.."
name = "semio-framework-os-mcp"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version.workspace = true
description = "Semio OS MCP gateway — dual-era JSON-RPC/MCP protocol core over stdio + Streamable HTTP, handle table, audit lane, shell bridge codec (packet P1b-http-handles-bridge, extending P1a-protocol-core: zero dependency on the plugin host/channel/actor crates)"

[package.metadata.semio]
role = "product"
id = "os-mcp"

[lints]
workspace = true

[lib]
path = "./🦀️.rs"
# 📚️ This crate carries no ``` doc examples (verified: zero fenced blocks in its sources), so the
# rustdoc pass has nothing to run — it only re-links every dependency rlib. With several sessions
# rebuilding `semio-framework`/`semio-framework-ui` concurrently in this shared tree, that link
# step intermittently fails on an rlib replaced mid-run. Skipping it removes a false failure
# without losing a single assertion; add real doc examples and this flips back on.
doctest = false

[[bin]]
name = "semio-os-mcp"
path = "../../🏗️bootstrap/⌨️entrypoint/🦀️.rs"

# ⏱️ Its own process: the binding law needs an empty compiled-code map to reach every phase.
[[test]]
name = "binding_cancellation_law"
path = "../../💡️inference/🧪️tests/⏱️binding-cancellation-law/🦀️.rs"

[[test]]
name = "compile_cancellation_law"
path = "../../🏠️workspace/🧪️tests/⏱️compile-cancellation-law/🦀️.rs"

[dependencies]
semio-framework-pack-json = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🎒️pack/🔤️json/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-diagnostic = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/⚠️diagnostic/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-dsl = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🗣️dsl/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-ui-locale = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🖱️ui/🌐️locale/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-schema-registry = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🧬️schema/📇️registry/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-value = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🌱️value/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
# 🔀️ O1 (drop dyn dispatch, dedyn-fw-os-misc): `#[dyn_enum]`/`dyn_enum_close!` — closes
# `GatewayBackend`'s implementor set (`NullBackend`, `HeadlessWorkspace`, `Arc<HeadlessWorkspace>`)
# into a real enum instead of `Box<dyn GatewayBackend>`. Same dependency shape `🔌️plugin`'s and
# `🛢️db`'s own Cargo.toml files already use.
semio-framework-dispatch-macros = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🔀️dispatch/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-dispatch-macros" }
# 🎫️ ticket 26/08/17/LLM-FIRST-OS-VIA-THE-SEMIO-OS-MCP-GATEWAY packet P2-catalog: the ONLY facet in
# this crate that depends on `semio-framework` is `🗂️catalog` (it compiles `CapabilityDefinition`s
# FROM `semio_framework::manifest::{PackageDescriptor, PluginManifest, AppDefinition, …}` — real types
# P3-manifest-schema landed). Every other facet (protocol/transport/🐙️handles/audit/bridge/errors/schema)
# stays framework-free, per D8/`📓️terra-P1a-report.md` §5 — this dependency does not change that.
semio-framework = { workspace = true }
semio-framework-async = { workspace = true }
semio-framework-schema = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🧬️schema/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-schema" }
# 🎫️ P2-catalog: `LocalizedLabel`/`SurfaceKind` are NOT re-exported at the `semio-framework` crate
# root (only `IconName`/`Locale`/`Terminology`/`ArtifactDialect` are — `../../📦️packages/🦀️rust/🦀️.rs` lines 15-16, 91-92);
# they live in `ui_wgpu::wgpu`, the same crate `🛂️manifest/🦀️.rs` itself imports them from
# (its own `use ui_wgpu::wgpu::{…, LocalizedLabel, …, SurfaceKind, …};`). `🧫️fixtures` constructs real
# `AppDefinition`/`WindowKindDefinition` values and needs both directly, so this crate depends on the
# SAME workspace-aliased crate manifest does, under its real Rust name (`semio_framework_ui`) — not a
# new external dependency, an existing internal one already one hop away.
semio-framework-ui = { workspace = true, features = ["wgpu"] }
schemars = "0.8.22"
serde = { workspace = true }
serde_json = { workspace = true }
# 🌐️ Streamable HTTP transport (P1b) — same version/feature style as 🌎️hub's own Cargo.toml, the
# repo's other axum+tokio product crate.
axum = { version = "0.8", features = ["ws"] }
tokio = { workspace = true, features = ["full"] }
# 🌊️ P1c: `SinkExt`/`StreamExt` (`WebSocket::split`) for the REAL `/bridge` connection loop
# (`🧵️bridge/🦀️.rs`'s `mod server::handle_socket`) — promoted from dev-only (P1b's websocket
# TEST used it) to a real dependency now that production code uses it too. Same version hub already
# depends on for its own websocket endpoints.
futures = "0.3"
# 🎫️ ticket 26/08/17/LLM-FIRST-OS-VIA-THE-SEMIO-OS-MCP-GATEWAY packet P7-headless-workspace: the
# `🏠️workspace` facet's real `store::sync::ArtifactHost`/`PersistenceBinding` binding layer — the
# `sync` feature is exactly what mounts `🏪️store/🔄️sync/🦀️.rs` into this crate
# (`💻️os/📦️packages/🦀️rust/🦀️.rs`'s own `#[cfg(feature = "sync")] pub mod sync;`), same crate
# `🏃️run`'s own Cargo.toml depends on. Relative path identical to `🏃️run`'s (same directory depth:
# both are `🔨️modules/<X>/📦️packages/🦀️rust`).
semio-framework-os-kernel = { path = "../../../../📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-os-kernel", features = ["sync", "ureq"] }
semio-framework-os-services = { workspace = true }
# 🎫️ P7-headless-workspace: `semio_framework_actor::ActorId` (aliased `RuntimeActorId` everywhere
# else in this tree) — needed directly because `semio-framework-plugin-host` only `use`s it
# internally, never `pub use`s it (verified: only `PackageId`/`PackageHash`/`PackageRef` are
# re-exported from that crate).
semio-framework-actor = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🎭️actor/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-actor" }
# 🎫️ P7-headless-workspace: real plugin actor activation (`WasmtimeRuntime`/`GuestRuntime`,
# `OpeningResolver`, `AppRouter`) — native-only, mirrors `🏃️run`'s own
# `[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies]` gate exactly (this crate never targets
# wasm32 itself — it is a stdio/HTTP server binary — but the gate is kept for consistency with the
# crate `semio-framework-plugin-host` itself requires it from).
framework_hash = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🔏️hash/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-hash" }

[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies]
semio-framework-plugin-host = { path = "../../../🔌️plugin/🖥️host/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-plugin-host" }
# 🎫️ ticket 26/09/18 slice M10: `document_backbone_binding` — the host↔guest CONTROL-PLANE codec for
# binding a guest instance's document backbone (`DocumentBackboneBindingCommandV1::encode` +
# `require_document_backbone_binding_receipt_v1`). A guest publishes `MessageEndpoint::Backbone`
# effects only once a host has bound one, so a gateway that wants its agent's committed envelopes to
# leave the process has to send that command. The wgpu renderer — the other real host — links this
# crate for exactly the same pair of functions (`🌉️ProgramBridge/🎯️targets/🧊️wgpu/🦀️.rs`
# `bind_document_backbone`); writing a second copy of the wire shape here instead would be the
# duplicate codec this repo forbids.
semio-framework-plugin = { path = "../../../🔌️plugin/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-plugin" }

[dev-dependencies]
# 🔌️ Drives the `🧵️bridge` `BridgeServer` skeleton's websocket upgrade end-to-end in tests — same
# version hub already uses for its own `os-hub` websocket tests (`🌎️hub/📦️packages/🦀️rust/Cargo.toml`).
tokio-tungstenite = "0.26"

# 🧭️ Own workspace root: never joins the repository's root workspace, whose root manifest is a shared,
# contended file.
#
# 🚫️ DEPENDS ON `lopdf` AND NOTHING ELSE — deliberately, and this is the entire point of the crate.
# The generator it replaces obtained both the mutated bytes AND the expected projection from this
# repository's own `semio-s-artifact-stdio-pdf-test-oracle`, which made `lopdf` a codec for our own answer:
# both halves of every comparison descended from one implementation, so a shared misreading of the PDF
# specification would produce two agreeing wrong answers. Here the mutation is applied through `lopdf`'s
# own public COS API and the projection is read back through it, so nothing in this repository predicts
# what the judge is judging.
#
# @see ../../../../../../../../../.🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️08/☀️27/SUBSET-SCOPED-EXTERNAL-ORACLE-MUTATION-TESTING/📓️pdf-fixtures-are-not-admissible-evidence.md
[workspace]

[[bin]]

manifests.source:
[package]
workspace = "../../../../../../.."
name = "semio-framework-os-infinite"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version.workspace = true
description = "OS infinite family — world/canvas/board Shape V2 glue"
build = "build.rs"

[package.metadata.semio]
role = "product"
id = "os-infinite"

[lints]
workspace = true

[features]
typegen = []
# 🌉️ Declared (but never enabled) so `🗺️surface/🏔️terrain/🦀️.rs`'s path-mounted
# `#[cfg(feature = "session-bindgen")]` wasm bridge doesn't trip `unexpected_cfgs` here — this
# crate path-mounts that file without the surface crate's own `session-bindgen` default, by design
# (avoids duplicate `TerrainSession` symbols linking surface+infinite into one cdylib).
session-bindgen = []

[lib]
name = "semio_framework_os_infinite"
crate-type = ["rlib"]
path = "🦀️.rs"

[dependencies]
semio-framework-pack-json = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🎒️pack/🔤️json/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-ui-locale = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🖱️ui/🌐️locale/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-value = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🌱️value/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-artifact-infinite-dag = { workspace = true }
semio-framework-os-kernel = { path = "../../../../📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-os-kernel" }
semio-framework-value-derive = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🌱️value/✨️derive/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-value-derive" }
semio-framework-job = { workspace = true }
# ⏯️ Decodes the `World3dScene.tool_run_trace` delta for the world's trace layer (`🌍️world/⏯️tool-run-trace`).
# Renderer-side only: ui/ui-scene/os-kernel/job never depend on it (`📓️wave-W0-A.md` cycle rule).
semio-framework-tool-run = { workspace = true }
# 🧱️ `boxed_fixed_slots` (the heap-first fixed slot table every retirement/admission registry in
# this crate builds through) plus the browser session bridges' async vocabulary. Unconditional: the
# helper is target-neutral and `semio-framework-job` already pulls this crate in on every target.
semio-framework-async = { workspace = true }
semio-framework = { path = "../../../../../../📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework" }
math = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🧮️math/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-math" }
geometry = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/📐️geometry/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-geometry" }
graph = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🕸️graph/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-graph" }
ui_styling = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🖱️ui/🎨️styling/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-ui-styling" }
semio-framework-ui-viewport = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🖱️ui/🪟️viewport/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio_framework_3d = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🧊️3d/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-3d" }
compiler = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/📚️compiler/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-compiler" }
serde = { version = "1.0.219", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1.0.140"
# 🔤️ First-party RFC 4648 codec — replaces the third-party `base64` crate for `icon_codec`'s
# `data:...;base64,...` decode (target-neutral: guest-reachable via `board_resolve_icon_kind`, see
# `🖼️canvas/🦀️.rs`). RUNTIME-DEPENDENCY-ELIMINATION-FOR-S-PLUGINS-AND-ARTIFACTS (26/09/01).
base64_codec = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🚪️io/🔤️base64/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-io-base64" }
# #️⃣ Unkeyed BLAKE3 for the `registerBrushMesh` upload identity (`🌍️world/🦀️.rs`) — byte-identical
# to the puzzle guest's own `brush_mesh_digest` and React's `puzzle3dBrushMeshDigest`, which is what
# lets the guest refuse a page run that does not reassemble into the announced mesh.
semio-framework-hash = { workspace = true }
# 🏔️ Required by the path-mounted `🗺️surface/🏔️terrain/🦀️.rs` above, which decodes
# Terrarium RGB-encoded elevation PNGs via the first-party `semio-framework-pixels` codec (no
# third-party runtime dependency) instead of `image`/`png`. That file is compiled into BOTH this
# crate and `semio-framework-surface` (mounted here by `#[path]` because surface depends on
# infinite, so a real dependency edge would be a cycle) — a shared source file needs the same
# dependency declared in every crate that mounts it. This removes `image`/`png`/`flate2`/
# `miniz_oxide`/`fdeflate`/`crc32fast`/`adler2`/`simd-adler32`/`byteorder-lite` from EVERY target's
# graph here, including `wasm32-wasip2` — this was the last unconditional `image` dependency in
# this manifest. RUNTIME-DEPENDENCY-ELIMINATION-FOR-S-PLUGINS-AND-ARTIFACTS (26/09/01).
semio-framework-pixels = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🔲️pixels/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-pixels" }

# ⚠️ RUNTIME-DEPENDENCY-ELIMINATION-FOR-S-PLUGINS-AND-ARTIFACTS (26/09/01): a prior attempt to move
# `vello`/`vello_svg`'s `wgpu` feature and `ui_wgpu`'s `wgpu-engine` feature behind a
# `not(target_env = "p2")` target table was REVERTED here because `🌍️world/🦀️.rs` named
# ~26 `ui_wgpu::wgpu` symbols (`Mesh3dFault`, `BoundedActionFault`, …) unconditionally, forcing
# `wgpu-engine` to stay on for every target including wasip2. That root cause is now fixed: those
# symbols were split into the target-neutral `ui_wgpu::draw_types`/`ui_wgpu::gizmo`/`action`/`input`
# tier (see `🖱️ui/🎯️targets/🧊️wgpu/🦀️.rs`'s top docstring), so `wgpu-engine` — and with it the
# real `wgpu` crate and its `wasm-bindgen-futures`/`js-sys`/`wasm-bindgen` chain — can finally be
# narrowed away from `wasm32-wasip2` here too. `gpu_session` (`🖼️canvas/🦀️.rs`, the only
# consumer of `vello::Renderer`/`util::RenderContext`/`vello::wgpu` in this crate) is already
# `#[cfg(all(target_arch = "wasm32", not(target_env = "p2")))]`-gated, so no wasip2 capability is
# lost.
#
# 🖊️ A later pass (`🔍️research/📓️vello-scene-first-party.md`) went further: `vello` itself (plus
# its `vello_encoding` buffer format and their font/SVG/codec transitive tail — `skrifa`,
# `read-fonts`, `font-types`, `png`, `guillotiere`, `moxcms`, `pxfm`, `svg_fmt`, `bytemuck`,
# `id-arena`, …) is now ALSO absent from the `wasm32-wasip2` table below — `canvas::Scene` no
# longer needs a real `vello::Scene` to build/measure/dispose commands, only to rasterize one,
# which `wasm32-wasip2` (a WASI Preview 2 guest with no GPU device access) never does. A later
# pass (`🔍️research/📓️kurbo-peniko-first-party.md`) went further still: `Scene`'s guest-reachable
# value types (`Cap`/`Join`/`Stroke`/`Color`/`FillRule`/`BlendMode`/`RasterImage` in
# `🖼️canvas/🦀️.rs`) are now first-party plain values, not `kurbo`/`peniko` wrappers, so `peniko`
# moved into the host/browser-only target table below, next to `vello`. The geometry follow-up
# reimplemented `Point`/`Vec2`/`Affine`/shapes/`BezPath`, including adaptive circle/arc/rounded-rect
# path generation, so `semio-framework-geometry` now keeps `kurbo` only as a test oracle and no
# longer brings `kurbo` or its transitive tail into `wasm32-wasip2`.
#
# 🔤️ `typst-assets` belongs to the standalone font tool. `typst`/`typst-svg`
# themselves were deleted outright (not narrowed) — grepped zero usage anywhere in this crate's
# source on ANY target, native included; they dragged in `usvg@0.45.1`/`biblatex`/`citationberg`/
# `comemo`/`ciborium`/… (100+ crates) for nothing. `usvg@0.46.0` (via `vello_svg`) is used by
# `🖼️canvas`'s icon/SVG-icon rendering (`svg_icon`/`SvgDocument`) AND by `mod text`'s map-label
# shaper (`append_label`/`label_byte_world_x`) — both traced this session
# (`🔍️research/📓️infinite-text-shaping.md`) as host/browser-only or unreachable on
# `wasm32-wasip2` (paint-tree-only, or behind flow's already-gated `wasm_session` bridge, or in
# `semio-framework-editor`, itself absent from every plugin's wasip2 dependency graph), so
# `vello_svg` moved out of the `wasm32-wasip2` target table entirely below.
[target.'cfg(not(all(target_arch = "wasm32", target_env = "p2")))'.dependencies]
ui_wgpu = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🖱️ui/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-ui", features = ["wgpu", "wgpu-engine"] }
vello = { version = "0.9.0", features = ["wgpu", "wgpu_default"] }
vello_svg = { version = "0.10.0", default-features = true, features = ["wgpu"] }
# 🎨️ Only the host-gated `SceneCommand::replay_into`/`Scene::vello_scene` rasterization boundary
# (`🖼️canvas/🦀️.rs`) still names `kurbo::`/`peniko::` directly — every guest-reachable value type
# is first-party now (`Cap`/`Join`/`Stroke`/`Color`/`FillRule`/`BlendMode`/`RasterImage`). Rust only
# exposes a crate's OWN direct dependencies by name, not a transitive dependency's, so this crate
# keeps its own `kurbo` edge to
# write `kurbo::Stroke`/`kurbo::Cap`/`kurbo::Join` at the conversion boundary — narrowing it to
# host-only correctly describes when this crate itself touches `kurbo`. Same exact
# `kurbo@0.13.1`/`peniko@0.6.1` instances `vello` itself resolves to (confirmed via
# `cargo tree -p peniko@0.6.1`/`-p kurbo@0.13.1`), so this is a dependency *edge* onto an
# already-locked package, not a new crate version. RUNTIME-DEPENDENCY-ELIMINATION-FOR-S-PLUGINS-AND-
# ARTIFACTS (26/09/01), `🔍️research/📓️kurbo-peniko-first-party.md`.
kurbo = "0.13.1"
peniko = "0.6.1"
# 🖼️ Real pixel decode for `icon_codec::decode_raster_icon_bytes`'s host/browser arm and
# `IconPaintCache::get_or_build`'s icon-painting path — both host-only on `wasm32-wasip2` (see
# `🖼️canvas/🦀️.rs`'s `raster_icon_bytes_to_rgba` and `➡️directed/🦀️.rs`'s
# `get_or_build` docstrings). RUNTIME-DEPENDENCY-ELIMINATION-FOR-S-PLUGINS-AND-ARTIFACTS (26/09/01).
image = { version = "0.25", default-features = false, features = ["png", "jpeg", "webp", "gif"] }

[target.'cfg(all(target_arch = "wasm32", target_env = "p2"))'.dependencies]
ui_wgpu = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🖱️ui/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-ui", features = ["wgpu"] }
# 🚫️ `vello` (and with it `vello_encoding`/`skrifa`/`read-fonts`/`font-types`/`png`/`flate2`/
# `miniz_oxide`/`fdeflate`/`crc32fast`/`adler2`/`simd-adler32`/`guillotiere`/`moxcms`/`pxfm`/
# `svg_fmt`/`bytemuck`/`bytemuck_derive`/`id-arena`/`static_assertions`/`core_maths`) deliberately
# absent here: `canvas::Scene`'s only unconditional job is to build, measure and incrementally
# dispose first-party `SceneCommand`s (see `🖼️canvas/🦀️.rs`) — real rasterization
# (`Scene::vello_scene`, building a real `vello::Scene` by replaying those commands) is reachable
# only from `gpu_session::render_frame`, already `not(all(wasm32, p2))`-gated, i.e. never on this
# target. `peniko`/`kurbo` are consequently ALSO absent from THIS crate's own dependency edges here
# (both moved into the host/browser-only table above): every value type `Scene`'s guest-reachable
# API (`fill`/`stroke`/`draw_image`/`append`/`push_layer`/`pop_layer`/…) needs is now a first-party
# plain value in `🖼️canvas/🦀️.rs` (`Cap`/`Join`/`Stroke`/`Color`/`FillRule`/`BlendMode`/
# `RasterImage`), converted to a real `peniko`/`kurbo` value only inside the host-gated
# `replay_into`. The geometry follow-up also removed `kurbo`'s final guest edge, so `kurbo`,
# `arrayvec`, `smallvec`, and `polycool` are absent from plugin `wasm32-wasip2` graphs.
# 🚫️ `vello_svg` (and with it `usvg`/`rustybuzz`(via usvg)/`fontdb`/…) deliberately absent here:
# `svg_icon`/`SvgDocument` (icon *painting*) and `mod text`'s `usvg`-shaped label shaper/painter
# (`append_label`/`append_label_tspans`/`label_byte_world_x`'s native arm) are both gated
# `not(all(wasm32, p2))` in `🖼️canvas/🦀️.rs` — every real caller traced this session is
# host/browser-only or unreachable on this target. `label_byte_world_x`'s `wasm32-wasip2` arm uses
# the character-width heuristic (`label_extent`/`label_advance`/`label_text_inset`) instead; icon
# painting's arm is `IconPaintCache::get_or_build`'s existing `None`. RUNTIME-DEPENDENCY-
# ELIMINATION-FOR-S-PLUGINS-AND-ARTIFACTS (26/09/01), `🔍️research/📓️infinite-text-shaping.md`.
# 📐️ Header/attribute-only dimension reader replacing `image`/`usvg` for this target's two
# dimension-only call sites (`icon_codec::decode_raster_icon_bytes`,
# `svg_icon::svg_icon_content_bounds_from_str`). RUNTIME-DEPENDENCY-ELIMINATION-FOR-S-PLUGINS-AND-
# ARTIFACTS (26/09/01), `🔍️research/📓️intrinsic-size-wiring.md`.
semio-framework-intrinsic-size = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/📏️intrinsic-size/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-intrinsic-size" }

# 🌉️ Browser-only session bridges (`gpu_session`/`wasm_session`/`wasm_bridge` in `🖼️canvas` and
# `🎲️board/…/🕸️dag`, plus the `wasm_bindgen_futures` alias their async-fn codegen needs). Excluded
# from `wasm32-wasip2` because `target_arch = "wasm32"` is TRUE for the WASI component target too —
# the wasip2 guest never attaches an `HtmlCanvasElement`. `dag_debug_log`/`pointer_event_now_ms`
# (same `🕸️dag` file) needed genuine wasip2 arms instead — see their docstrings.
[target.'cfg(all(target_arch = "wasm32", not(target_env = "p2")))'.dependencies]
js-sys = "0.3.83"
wasm-bindgen = "0.2.106"
web-sys = { version = "0.3.98", features = ["HtmlCanvasElement", "Window", "Request", "RequestInit", "RequestMode", "Response", "console"] }

[build-dependencies]
serde = { version = "1.0.219", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1.0.140"

[dev-dependencies]
semio-framework-async-macros = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/⏳️async/✨️macros/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }

# The DOCUMENT-level reader for this subset's twelve `create-*`/`delete-*` resource kinds. `three`
# builds a scene graph and never sees an unreferenced resource; `@gltf-transform/core` folds glTF's
# separate `images`, `samplers` and `textures` arrays into one `Texture` concept and exposes no

# what lets `create-image` be told apart from `create-texture`.
[workspace]

version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
publish = false

[[bin]]
name = "reader"
path = "../../🦀️.rs"

[dependencies]
gltf = { version = "1.4", default-features = false, features = ["import", "utils", "names"] }

manifests.source:
[package]
workspace = "../../../../../../.."
name = "semio-framework-os-services"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version.workspace = true
description = "Where tokio lives, and nowhere else. Host-side async services built ON TOP of semio-framework-async's HostAsyncRuntime/WorkerPool: the runtime impl (TokioHostRuntime, re-hosted onto the shared process-wide WorkerPool by INTERACTIVE-JOB-RUNTIME-REFACTOR Phase 1 packet P1b), scope table, a single host timer wheel, a bounded blocking-compute pool, an HTTP connection pool, a storage scheduler and an indexed event router. tokio is confined to this crate (sync/macros only — no owned thread pool) — its public API names only semio-framework-async types and this crate's own types, never a tokio type, exactly as wasmtime is confined behind GuestRuntime in the plugin-host crate (design ticket 26/08/17/MICROKERNEL-POOLED-ACTOR-PLUGIN-RUNTIME, packet R2)."

[package.metadata.semio]
role = "product"
id = "os-services"

[lints]
workspace = true

[lib]
name = "semio_framework_os_services"
path = "🦀️.rs"

[dependencies]
# 🧵️ INTERACTIVE-JOB-RUNTIME-REFACTOR Phase 1 packet P1b: `entrypoint` unlocks
# `semio_framework_async::block_on` — the future-polling bridge every `WorkerPool` job submitted by
# `ScopeTable::spawn_scoped`/`TimerWheel::spawn_driver`/`HttpPool::spawn_refill_driver` uses to turn
# its own worker into that task's executor (see `🦀️.rs`'s module doc), and
# `TokioHostRuntime::block_on`'s own inherent bridge delegates to directly. Workspace-internal
# feature flag on an already-present dependency, not a new third-party dependency.
semio-framework-async = { workspace = true, features = ["entrypoint"] }
# 🎭️ MICROKERNEL-POOLED-ACTOR-PLUGIN-RUNTIME (coordinator correction on packet R2): `PackageId`
# (per-plugin quota identity) and `ActorId` (per-actor identity) are consumed from here rather than
# reinvented locally — this crate is `os-services`, not domain-neutral, so unlike
# `semio-framework-async` it should NOT keep its own parallel newtypes for the same concepts the
# actor crate already owns. Pure crate (no tokio, no threads, builds for wasm32-unknown-unknown), so
# this costs no platform coupling; `🔌️plugin/🖥️host` already depends on it the same way.
semio-framework-actor = { workspace = true }
semio-framework-job = { workspace = true }
# 🧵️ INTERACTIVE-JOB-RUNTIME-REFACTOR Phase 1 packet P1b: this crate no longer builds a
# `tokio::runtime::Runtime` of any flavor — `semio_framework_async::WorkerPool` (via
# `global_worker_pool`) is now the ONE owner of real OS threads a `TokioHostRuntime` and every
# service built on it schedules onto (see `🦀️.rs`'s module doc's tokio-containment note).
# The remaining tokio surface is `sync` (a pure, runtime-context-free `oneshot`/`Semaphore`/`Notify`
# — none of the three need an entered `Runtime` to function) and `macros` (the `select!` macro, also
# runtime-context-free — it is plain manual polling, not a scheduler). `rt`/`rt-multi-thread`/`time`
# are gone: their old callers (`tokio::runtime::Builder`, `tokio::task::JoinSet`,
# `tokio::time::sleep`/`sleep_until`/`timeout`) are replaced by `WorkerPool`/its `TimerWheel`
# throughout.
tokio = { workspace = true, features = ["sync", "macros"] }

[dev-dependencies]
# 🧵️ INTERACTIVE-JOB-RUNTIME-REFACTOR Phase 1 packet P1b: `testkit` (and `ManualRuntime`, the
# deterministic-clock `HostAsyncRuntime` test double it gates) is DROPPED here — every test that used
# to drive `ManualRuntime`'s injected clock now drives a real `semio_framework_async::WorkerPool` on
# the real wall clock instead (`TimerWheel::spawn_driver`/`HttpPool::spawn_refill_driver` no longer
# accept a generic `R: HostAsyncRuntime` at all — see `🦀️.rs`), so nothing in this crate's
# own suite constructs a `ManualRuntime` any more. `entrypoint` is already unified in from the main
# dependency above (`cargo test` merges regular and dev-dependency features for one crate into a
# single compilation), listed again here only so this crate's OWN test suite's need for `block_on` is
# self-documenting from this line alone.
semio-framework-async = { workspace = true, features = ["entrypoint"] }
tokio = { workspace = true, features = ["sync", "macros"] }
# 🧵️ gate-services (universal-async residue sweep): every `HostAsyncRuntime` method this file's
# tests exercise is `async fn` — every test needs a real async-test harness. Path dependency, same
# pattern `🎭️actor`'s Cargo.toml already uses for this macro crate.
semio-framework-async-macros = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/⏳️async/✨️macros/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
serde_json = { workspace = true }

manifests.name: semio-framework-os-kernel-db
manifests.source:
[package]
workspace = "../../../../../../.."
name = "semio-framework-os-kernel-db"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version.workspace = true
description = "Db facade — Shape V2 #[path] glue over owner-tree db components"

[package.metadata.semio]
role = "product"
id = "os-db"

[lints]
workspace = true

[lib]
name = "db"
path = "🦀️.rs"

[features]
default = ["fs", "deflate"]
fs = []
deflate = []
cluster = []
otel = []
# 🔌️ Each backend feature pulls in its own driver dep — mirrors `🌎️hub/📦️packages/🦀️rust/Cargo.toml`'s
# same-named features one level up, which forward into these.
sqlite = ["dep:rusqlite"]
postgres = ["dep:sqlx", "dep:tokio"]
neo4j = ["dep:neo4rs", "dep:tokio"]
# 🗝️ The claimed-shared-server test support (`db_storage::claimed_backend`) for OTHER crates' live laws (the hub's
# directory lanes): never in a runtime build, only in their `[dev-dependencies]`.
claimed-backend-laws = []

[dependencies]
semio-framework-diagnostic = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/⚠️diagnostic/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-value = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🌱️value/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-os-kernel = { path = "../../../../📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-os-kernel" }
semio-framework-replication = { workspace = true }
# 🔌️ `db_storage`'s schema-first task family crosses the sync/async boundary through the
# process-wide `WorkerPool` I/O lane; `FsStorage`/`db_storage_sqlite::SqliteStorage` dispatch
# their typed, retained operations there, and
# this crate names no concrete executor (no `tokio`, no `futures`) anywhere EXCEPT the one bounded
# runtime `db_storage_driver_runtime` owns for the external drivers that are bound to one — see that
# module's doc and `db_storage::DbIoAsyncDriverRuntime`. See `db_storage`'s module doc ("Async-first").
semio-framework-async = { workspace = true }
# 🔌️ Phase 1 (`26/08/20/INTERACTIVE-JOB-RUNTIME-REFACTOR`): `db_storage`'s blocking bridge submits
# to the process-wide `WorkerPool` on `Lane::Io` and reports its queue depth through this crate's
# `QueueCounter` for the Phase 1 exit gate. Workspace-internal, not a new third-party dependency.
semio-framework-trace = { workspace = true }
serde = { version = "1.0.219", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1.0.140"
semio-framework-hash = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🔏️hash/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies]
rusqlite = { version = "0.38.0", features = ["blob", "bundled"], optional = true }
# 🔌️ Same `sqlx-core`/`sqlx-postgres` major version `🌎️hub/📦️packages/🦀️rust/Cargo.toml` pins for its
# own directory backend, so the workspace resolves one `sqlx` line, not two. `runtime-tokio`
# selects sqlx's internal executor binding at ITS compile time — it does not require this crate to
# depend on `tokio` for its own sake. It does need one at RUNTIME: `sqlx` demands its runtime's
# thread-local context at poll time, and `db_storage`'s async-native drivers are dispatched from
# `Lane::Io` of the tokio-free `WorkerPool`, so the futures are polled on the bounded runtime
# `db_storage_driver_runtime` owns and never on a pool worker (measured abort: ticket 26/09/18 D4).
sqlx = { version = "0.8", default-features = false, features = ["runtime-tokio", "tls-rustls", "postgres"], optional = true }
neo4rs = { version = "0.8", optional = true }
# 🧵️ ONLY for `db_storage_driver_runtime` — the bounded, never-shut-down runtime the `sqlx`/`neo4rs`
# drivers above are polled on, behind `db_storage::DbIoAsyncDriverRuntime`. Enabled exactly by the
# `postgres`/`neo4j` features, i.e. only when a driver that requires one is actually linked. `rt`
# + `rt-multi-thread` build it, `net`/`time` give the drivers their reactor and timers.
tokio = { workspace = true, features = ["rt", "rt-multi-thread", "net", "time"], optional = true }

[dev-dependencies]
semio-framework-os-kernel = { path = "../../../../📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-os-kernel", features = ["durable-group-testing"] }
# 🎒️ Renamed on purpose: this package's lib target is named `pack`, and cargo derives a dependency's
# extern name from the LIB name unless the dependency key renames it — so plain
# `semio-framework-pack` arrives as `pack`, which this crate has already bound to the os-kernel
# (`extern crate semio_framework_os_kernel as pack`). The key then loses and `🦀️.rs`'s
# `pub use semio_framework_pack::corruption_testing` stops resolving, taking the whole test target
# with it. Naming the key `semio_framework_pack` is what makes cargo rename it.
semio_framework_pack = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🎒️pack/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-pack", features = ["corruption-testing"] }
semio-framework-async-macros = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/⏳️async/✨️macros/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-async = { workspace = true, features = ["testkit"] }

[features]

component-guest = []
component-extension-guest = []
# ⏳️ MICROKERNEL-POOLED-ACTOR-PLUGIN-RUNTIME (W6-A, jobs-runtime → B1 world-collapse): selects the
# guest-side DIRECT host-import path, where a job body awaits `host-async` rather than emitting an
# effect and waiting for its completion event. Since the collapse both paths live in the SAME
# `world actor` (there is no second world), so this gates a calling convention, not a world. It MUST be declared even while no consumer enables it yet —
# an undeclared feature makes every `#[cfg(feature = "component-guest-async")]` block silently unreachable,
# so the code inside is never type-checked by any build (the standing `cfg`-gated-code trap). `JobCtx::host()`
# lives behind exactly this gate.
component-guest-async = []
artifact-app-testing = []

[dependencies]
semio-framework-pack-json = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🎒️pack/🔤️json/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }

semio-framework-dsl = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🗣️dsl/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-ui-locale = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🖱️ui/🌐️locale/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-schema-state = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🧬️schema/📶️state/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }

semio-framework-schema-registry = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🧬️schema/📇️registry/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework-2d = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/◻️2d/📦️packages/🦀️rust", default-features = false }
semio-framework-value = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/🌱️value/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
semio-framework = { path = "../../../../../../../🧰️framework/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework" }
semio-framework-async = { path = "../../../../../../../🧰️framework/🔨️modules/⏳️async/📦️packages/🦀️rust", package = "semio-framework-async" }

# folds `ToolRunTick`s and publishes one `Edit` at finalize; the pure contract crate never depends back on this one.
